services: Advocacy for laws and regulations that support sustainable water supplies.
Regional water resource planning and problem-solving among member municipalities.
Information, tools, and assistance to help residents and businesses conserve water.
audiences: Municipal staff, city managers, and elected officials.
Residents and businesses in member communities.
Policymakers working on Arizona water issues.
service_area: Member municipalities include Phoenix, Peoria, Scottsdale, Glendale, Avondale, Goodyear, Tempe, Mesa, Gilbert, and Chandler.
Official history states members serve roughly 3.7 million people.
confirmed_facts.address: 3003 N. Central Ave., Suite 1550, Phoenix, AZ 85012
confirmed_facts.hours: Public office hours were not found on the official pages reviewed; official contact page notes visitor parking validation at 3003 N Central parking garage.
differentiators: Official story says AMWUA was incorporated in 1969 by Mesa, Phoenix, and Scottsdale, with Glendale and Tempe joining early.
Official mission focuses on assured, safe, and sustainable water supplies for member communities.
Official site says AMWUA has been involved in significant Arizona water management issues over the past half-century.
trust_signals: Official site lists address, phone, and info@amwua.org.
Official governance page describes a board of directors made up of mayors and councilmembers from member municipalities.
Nonprofit listing references IRS public 990 data and purpose.
products: Landscape, garden, DIY, and professional conservation resources.
pricing_notes: No public consumer pricing was found; AMWUA is an association/policy organization rather than a retail water provider.
